title: Axon macos-acceptance-v1
description: Measured acceptance of macOS PID-targeted synthetic input, one row per target and action. Rows are implementation-neutral: they record what macOS did, keyed on identity facts a backend can read at dispatch time, so a delivery implementation in any language can consume them without inheriting the campaign's own assumptions. A row is evidence, not a permission: the consumer decides what to authorize, and an absent row authorizes nothing.

schemaVersion.description: This contract's identity. Within macos-acceptance-v1 producers may add rows and campaigns; removing a required field or changing what a verdict means requires a new major.

generatedAt.description: When this document was last written. Distinct from a campaign's measuredAt: regenerating the file does not re-measure anything.

campaigns.description: The measurement sessions the rows were earned in. A row cites one by id rather than repeating its machine and permission facts, so two rows measured together cannot disagree about the bench they ran on.

rows.description: One row per target and action. Rows are app-specific unless macOS offers a stable generic signature, because a family-wide entry claims more than any single application can prove.

measuredAt.description: When the measurements were taken, not when the file was written.

machine.description: Hardware model and architecture of the bench.

session.description: What kind of session this was: an interactive desktop with a logged-in user, or something else. PID-targeted input cannot be measured without one.

harness.description: The commit or description of the harness that produced this campaign.

rawEvidence.description: Path, relative to this directory, of the unnormalized record this run wrote for diagnosis. Not committed: it is bench-local and each run writes its own.

permissions.description: The permission state of the posting process. Missing permission makes every trial blocked rather than refused: macOS drops posted events from an untrusted process silently, which from the sending side is indistinguishable from a target declining them.

automation.description: Per-target Automation (Apple Events) state, where it was needed. Recorded per bundle identifier because macOS grants it that way.

id.description: The stable identifier a Rust source comment or a refusal detail cites. It names the target, the action and the campaign date so a citation stays legible without the file open beside it.

action.description: Click evidence never authorizes keyboard, drag or scroll: each action is measured and recorded on its own.

mechanism.description: The delivery mechanism measured. Only PID-targeted Core Graphics posting is in scope here.

variant.description: The exact construction posted, including the event source and the down/up hold. A row speaks only for the variant it names, because an application that ignores one construction may act on another.

verdict.description: accepted: the target acted while the decoy held the foreground and the real pointer did not move. refused: the post was accepted by macOS and the target did nothing. blocked: the trial could not establish its own preconditions, so it says nothing about the target. unavailable: the target software was not present.

reason.description: Why this verdict, in a sentence a refusal detail can carry.

rawEvidence.description: Names the trial in the unnormalized record its run wrote, as a path and a fragment. That record is written on the bench that ran the campaign and is not committed; this is a pointer for whoever still has that machine, and not a link. Everything a verdict rests on is carried by the row itself.

remeasureWhen.description: What invalidates this row. Application and OS releases invalidate it; commits to this repository do not.

kind.description: What the target is built on, as a description rather than as a key. A consumer keys on identity, never on this.

identity.description: The dispatch-time identity candidates: what a backend holding only a process identifier can actually read about the target before it posts anything.

versionSeries.description: The major.minor prefix an entry would key on, because that is the granularity an application's own version string supports.

runtimeSignature.description: An engine or runtime version, only when it is genuinely readable from the target's own bundle at dispatch time. Null where macOS publishes nothing, which is itself the finding that keeps a row app-specific.

readableAtDispatch.description: Whether every identity fact above was read from the running process rather than from the campaign's own knowledge of what it launched.

source.description: The API path the identity was read through.

dispatchAccepted.description: Whether the Core Graphics post completed. This is dispatch evidence and nothing more: CGEventPostToPid returns no status, so a completed post never proves the target received or acted on anything.

targetMutated.description: Whether the target itself changed: a control moved, a page navigated, a field echoed. This is the only evidence that can license an accepted verdict.

eventReachedTarget.description: Whether the target's process observed the event arriving, where the target can report that. It separates 'never delivered' from 'delivered and declined', which the sending side cannot tell apart.

decoyFrontmost.description: Whether a decoy application held the foreground across the dispatch. Without this the target may simply have been receiving ordinary input.

ownershipProved.description: Whether the target owned the topmost ordinary window at the dispatch coordinate, checked immediately before posting.

controls.description: The two foreground controls that bracket a dispatch. A trial whose control did not act is measuring the campaign rather than the target, and is blocked rather than refused.

freshState.description: Whether this trial ran against a target that had received no prior synthetic input. A keyboard verdict may only be earned on a fresh target: a window that was just clicked can route keys it would otherwise drop.
